occurrences.passage: \textbf{C3.} We show how peak-limit rankings change with the historical reference and breach assessment in these observed forecasting tasks. We compare same-history and shorter-history rolling controls across three windows with previously examined outcomes, using established score diagrams and error-weight preferences. For the distinct long-horizon legacy comparison, the preferred report reverses at a penalty ratio of about 20.6:1. Where the endpoint lineage evaluates intervals and Ehm et al. (2016) develop general score comparisons, we connect these diagnostics to monitoring limits with completed path labels. Sections~\ref{sec:evaluation}--\ref{sec:implications} support a four-part checklist: use matured labels, separate history and model changes, report scores with breaches, and check stability across periods and related series.

Financial path-risk studies establish that a within-period extreme can matter more than the value observed at the end of the period. MaxVaR evaluates the worst cumulative portfolio return under a fixed portfolio and diffusion assumptions, including a conversion from endpoint probabilities to path risk \citep{boudoukh2004}. The payment-liquidity thesis studies conditional maximum deficits using a different path-risk target and confidential transactions \citep{hoogen2017}. Related settlement studies examine tail liquidity needs and collateral requirements in their respective payment systems \citep{petrunia2019,arjani2020}. Duffie and colleagues analyze dealer capacity and Treasury-market functioning, with additional out-of-sample PnL quantile comparisons in their appendix \citep{duffie2023}. Our empirical contribution concerns matched forecasts of the present peak-position target across the FX record and related public position aggregates.

Quantile estimation and evaluation supply established tools for comparing conditional peak forecasts against historical rules on a shared response. Regression quantiles target asymmetric forecast errors, providing the basic statistical building block for the proposed conditional reports \citep{koenker1978}. Conditional autoregressive quantiles and quantile forests offer additional conditioning structures for forecasting applications that differ in response, predictors and estimation \citep{engle2004,meinshausen2006}. Learning-curve research documents diverse and sometimes nonmonotone relationships between training size and predictive performance across methods and data conditions \citep{viering2023}. Our fixed-period curves compare relative loss against a historical reference that also changes with training history, differing from an independent-sample expected-risk curve. Consistent scoring tools explain ranking differences across evaluation questions \citep{gneiting2011,ehm2016}; Table~\ref{tab:literature} locates the shared peak target, mature labels and matched reference design.

The inclusion of the issue position matters because a feasible peak limit must already cover the exposure observed at the forecast origin. Figure~\ref{fig:example} shows a real window selected by a fixed chronological rule, with an endpoint inside the limit and an earlier peak outside it. A successful endpoint interval can therefore answer a different risk question from a successful report for the full sampled peak. We evaluate the latter through pinball loss and count a breach precisely when the observed peak strictly exceeds the reported limit. This report monitors sampled net inventory; its known floor neither measures settlement cash needs nor establishes an optimal operating limit.

The Supplement provides the complete prior and later comparison inventories, the exact evaluation clocks, numerical checks, and all incomplete or unsuccessful procedures. We report sensitivity to bandwidth, adjustment family, target level, and state definition as separate diagnostic questions within their specified scopes. The subsequent interpretation follows the same sequence: establish the reference and sample, compare losses, examine breaches, and assess stability across periods. A credible peak-limit gain must survive this sequence with its benchmark and its information set stated clearly.

The controlled mean-reverting level study with GARCH innovations rejects the proposed narrow-regime explanation \citep{bollerslev1986}. Each regression shows clear gains in only 2 of 12 target cells. Both also show clear gains in 6 of 60 outside cells, including homoskedastic and longer-horizon cases. The experiment uses 32 independent repetition streams with common innovations across conditions and 72 evaluation issues per repetition. Figure~\ref{fig:mechanism} places the saved comparisons on a common history-to-horizon coordinate. These specified processes therefore do not establish a universal history, volatility or horizon boundary.

\paragraph{Code availability.} Code, saved results and version-specific reproduction instructions are available at \url{https://github.com/ByronLi0207/financial-mathematics-paper-20261020}. The earlier controlled grid, same-dealer daily contrast and overlapping backcast remain complete. This revision adds the post hoc coordinate comparison, pre-run simulation screen and fixed-period financial learning curve, with all counterexamples and unavailable prediction statuses visible. The completed results include adverse, failed and unavailable cases; arithmetic readback establishes artifact consistency rather than independent scientific replication.
